title: Godot fails to include FrameworkReference included assemblies outside of exports
body:
### Tested versions

Reproduced when testing on:
- v4.7.stable.mono
- v4.5.1.stable.mono
- W4 4.5 fork.

### System information

Windows 11. .Net SDKs for 10 and 8 installed

### Issue description

Godot editor/debug runs do not appear to resolve assemblies provided by framework references declared in the project .csproj, such as:

`<FrameworkReference Include="Microsoft.AspNetCore.App" />`

This affects runs from the editor, and also launches through external tooling such as IDEs. The generated debug output folder does not contain the framework assemblies, although this may be expected for `FrameworkReference` assemblies if they are intended to be resolved from the platform’s shared framework under the .NET root. However, that resolution does not occur, so attempting to use APIs from the framework reference throws a FileNotFoundException.

For example, a project targeting `net8.0` with a `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App` framework reference fails when attempting to load `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions` 

When doing a full export (via the Project->Export Menu), the framework assemblies are correctly included and will load at runtime as expected.

This is likely a duplicate of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/112701, but that seems stale and did not include a minimal repro project.

Probing should resolve the `FrameworkReference` elements at runtime (or have them included in the output for debug builds too, if that's the intended design). Until then, the issue can be worked around by either:

**Method 1: Updating GodotSharp's `runtimeconfig.json`**

You can manually include the needed framework reference by updating `GodotPlugins.runtimeconfig.json`.  For example, by adding:

```
    "frameworks": [
      {
        "name": "Microsoft.NETCore.App",
        "version": "8.0.0"
      },
      {
        "name": "Microsoft.AspNetCore.App",
        "version": "8.0.0"
      }
    ],
```

Ideally, this wouldn't be necessary and could be done at a project level, but this won't be available unless https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/72333 is completed. Until then, every time you upgrade Godot (even minor versions), you'll lose the update and have to reapply it. This is very brittle (and has tripped us up multiple times).

**Method 2: Custom Resolver**

The other alternative is to implement a custom runtime resolver for the affected assemblies that is included only in debug builds. 

Example resolver that we successfully tested: [SharedFrameworkResolver.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29576191/SharedFrameworkResolver.zip)

This successfully resolves the missing assemblies in editor/debug runs. However, this is also brittle because the project has to manually know which framework assemblies/folders to probe. We tested this successfully behind debug/preprocessor guards, but it's quite an ugly workaround.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Include a `FrameworkReference` element for a shared system assembly, e.g.  `<FrameworkReference Include="Microsoft.AspNetCore.App" />`
2. Use something in that assembly.
3. Launch a debug build from the editor, and have it fail to resolve the assembly (you can also note it missing from the build output).

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[framework-reference-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29575788/framework-reference-test.zip)
